sentences.text: Ichthyovenator is a genus of dinosaur belonging to the family Spinosauridae.

While it was initially placed in the subfamily Baryonychinae, recent studies classify it as a primitive member of the subfamily Spinosaurinae, a grouping supported by its tall dorsal sail and basal position within the family.

Although no skull remains of Ichthyovenator exist, related spinosaurids possessed elongated, narrow snouts similar to modern crocodilians, and Ichthyovenator itself had conical, straight teeth that lacked serrations.

The animal featured a blade-like ilium measuring 92 cm long, which was proportionally longer relative to its 65 cm pubic bone than in any other known large theropod, and it had elongated neural spines forming a sail on its back with a particular wavy curvature and division into two parts over the hips.
In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Ichthyovenator was approximately 8.5 meters long and weighed 2 tons.
Researchers identified the thirteenth dorsal neural spine as being 410% the length of the centrum, highlighting the extreme proportions of its sail structure.
Its ilium was proportionally longer relative to its pubic bone than in any other known large theropod.
Fossils of Ichthyovenator were collected from the Grès supérieurs Formation in the Savannakhet Basin, specifically at Ban Kalum in Savannakhet Province, Laos.
The first fossils were discovered in 2010, and the initial specimens were designated catalogue numbers MDS BK10-01 to 15, with the holotype found in the same formation.

Ichthyovenator likely had a diet mainly consisting of aquatic prey, as the morphology of its jaws and teeth has led many paleontologists to believe spinosaurids were primarily piscivorous, though evidence such as iguanodontid bones in a Baryonyx specimen suggests some spinosaurids may have had a more generalist diet including larger prey.

Spinosaurids like Ichthyovenator likely had semiaquatic lifestyles, inferred from limb bone density and oxygen isotope ratios in their teeth, and although no limb bones of Ichthyovenator are known, related spinosaurids had enlarged thumb claws used for hunting and processing prey.
In 2019, Arden and colleagues suggested Ichthyovenator's short pelvis and elongated tail spines indicate spinosaurids used their tails for underwater propulsion.
Ichthyovenator lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago, approximately 125 million years ago, in what is now Asia.

It is debated whether Ichthyovenator's sail was used for sexual display or species recognition, with researcher Darren Naish favoring sexual selection over species recognition in 2013, noting it evolved independently without close relatives.
It is also debated whether the Chinese species Sinopliosaurus fusuiensis represents the same animal as the Thai genus Siamosaurus.

In 2014, Allain reclassified Ichthyovenator into the subfamily Spinosaurinae based on tooth morphology and vertebral similarities, but a 2015 study suggested that Ichthyovenator possesses traits of both subfamilies, implying the distinction between Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae may be unclear.
Researcher Mickey Mortimer hypothesized that Ichthyovenator might not be a spinosaurid at all, but rather a carcarodontosaurid.
